**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – nobody has documented the first-touch journey (induction format, fitness assessment, liability waivers, expectation-setting); this directly affects retention and safety compliance
- **Member Checklins & Retention** – no systematic process for reaching out to at-risk members, dormant accounts, or post-pause re-engagement
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no win-back protocol, exit interview, or data capture on why members leave
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no career progression, competency ladder, or upskilling pathway for coaches; limits retention and quality consistency
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no standardised way to measure coaching delivery, class pacing, member engagement, or safety enforcement
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – critical gap; you're storing member data without documented data handling, consent, or retention protocols
- **Referral Programme** – no documented mechanics (incentives, tracking, payout, messaging) even though referrals are cheap acquisition
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – no clarity on what coaches actually own week-to-week (programming, social content, 1-on-1 outreach, feedback cycles)
- **30 Day Goals & Member Outcomes** – no process for goal-setting, tracking, or celebrating progress; kills engagement
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – no escalation path for common complaints (injured mid-class, billing issues, coach conflicts, cleanliness)

**Needs updating**

- **Coach SOPs** – likely missing: accountability for member touchpoints outside class, how coaches feed back on member progress to retention team, standards for correcting unsafe form mid-class
- **Facilities SOPs** – missing deep-clean schedules, equipment maintenance logs, emergency incident reporting (what happens when someone gets injured?)

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your revenue anchor — tier your memberships NOW**
Don't overthink this. List your THREE membership levels (Basic/Standard/Premium or similar), price them, and lock them in. Grace: what's your current pricing? Use that as your floor. Add one tier above at +30-40% (includes class priority + 1 coaching session/month). This creates an immediate upsell path. Have this done in 2 days max — perfectionism kills momentum.

**2. Create TWO separate docs — coach-facing and member-facing**
Coaches need to see: what packages they can sell, commission structure, what's bundled vs. à la carte, upsell sequences. Members see: clean, benefit-focused descriptions (not feature dumps). Use Canva or a simple Google Doc template — not a 20-page PDF. Coaches won't read it; members won't finish it.

**3. Audit what you actually deliver vs. what you're promising**
Walk through a typical week. What classes run? How many 1-on-1 sessions are realistic? What's your actual coach capacity? Your menu must reflect real capacity, not wishful thinking. If you promise it, price it to ensure profitability.

**4. Price coaching sessions as standalone products with urgency**
Don't bury them. "5-Class Package: £75" and "1 Coaching Session: £40" (or whatever works). Add a scarcity angle: "Coaching slots limited to X per coach per week." This drives fast decisions from members.

**What's your current pricing structure? That changes the priority order here.**

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO REVIEW

## REVENUE — URGENT PRIORITY: ARREST MEMBER DILUTION & MAXIMISE YIELD

• **Revenue per member has collapsed from £142 (July) to £98 (August) — a 31% drop on a larger member base (165 vs 139).** This is the single biggest red flag. August added 26 members but revenue fell £3.6k. Either (a) new members are on introductory/discounted rates and aren't converting to full-price, or (b) churn is happening among higher-paying tiers. Pull TeamUp reports on cohort pricing and tenure — if intros/discounts are >30 days, shorten to 2 weeks and enforce upgrade pricing within 14 days. This is costing you ~£2,400/month in visible leakage.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May then normalised** — but that May spike (17 members lost) needs postmortem: were those post-intro defaults, or seasonal? Cross-reference with payment failures in GoCardless. If it's payment friction, implement Stripe recurring + auto-retry within 48 hours.

• **Last 3 months (June–Aug) average £17.4k/month revenue vs prior 3 (March–May) at £15.4k — growth is real (+13%), but it's entirely member count, not pricing power.** You're at 165 members now. Calculate LTV: if average member pays for 8 months and then churns, your LTV is ~£780–£1,040. Acquisition cost per new member (marketing + onboarding time) should be <£150 to justify. Are you tracking this? If not, start now.

• **Launch a tiered upsell: move from single "membership" to Membership + PT add-on (£40–£60/month) + nutrition/class-pass bundles (£15–£25).** At 165 members, even 20% uptake on a £50 add-on is +£1,650/month revenue. August's revenue/member (£98) should be closer to £120–£130 once the cohort matures and add-ons gain traction.
